speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the breast mass you've noticed, including when you first found it and if it causes any pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the mass feel hard or rubbery, and is it fixed to the surrounding tissue or mobile? Have you experienced any nipple discharge, skin changes like dimpling or redness, or swollen lymph nodes in your armpit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rapid growth and your age, I need to check for systemic signs; have you experienced any unexplained fevers, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss? I will also request an ultrasound to characterize the mass and a biopsy for definitive diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Breast_Ultrasound, Core_Needle_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy showing leaf-like structures with stromal overgrowth is highly suggestive of a phyllodes tumor. To help distinguish between benign, borderline, or malignant variants, do you have any personal or family history of breast cancer or other neoplasms?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No family history of breast cancer. Social history: Non-smoker, moderate alcohol use. Elementary school teacher.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation and histology are classic for a phyllodes tumor, so I will proceed with the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes tumor
